decisionBox.changed: Position flips from midday's ADD to TAKE_PROFIT, and this is the first trim of the day. Nothing about the technical read got worse - price is above every EMA on 15m, 1H, 4H and daily, the 1H MACD has crossed back bullish and the day printed a new 24h high. What changed is the wallet's shape against the calendar. Midday's fourth consecutive add left 3.88 USDT of cash against roughly 199 USDT of spot, so the book is about 98 percent invested going into a six-and-a-half-hour Sunday-night gap with no ability to react. Trimming 12 percent of the spot core at 80,141.4 - roughly 1,644 points above the 78,496.88 average entry - rebuilds dry powder for the midnight and morning sessions without touching the long-term thesis. It is a liquidity decision, not a bearish one.

overnightRisk: Three specific things, in order of how much they should worry the wallet. ONE - the move that produced the 80,555.4 high was forced short covering, not accumulation, and the fuel is gone. 813,202 USD of liquidations in the 80,500 bucket across 96 fills, 100 percent of it SHORT, printed inside a 41-minute window ending 00:19 UTC; price has already faded 414 points off that high in the roughly 25 minutes since. Squeezes that exhaust their own fuel routinely give back the whole extension, and the first real support underneath is not until the 1H EMA20 at 79,909.63 and then the 79,644.9 session low. TWO - it is Sunday night. The US spot ETF channel is shut until Monday, Farside's confirmed record still ends at 04 September, and OKX 24h spot volume is 2,985 BTC. Thin books mean the 500-point move that just happened up can happen down on the same size, and the wallet cannot respond for six and a half hours. THREE - a live geopolitical headline: CNBC's front page at the time of this read leads with Asia-Pacific markets opening higher as investors assess renewed Middle East hostilities. That cuts both ways for BTC - Brent closed Friday at 92.32, up 0.75 percent, and an oil-led risk shock has historically hit crypto before it helps it - but the point is that the tape will be reacting to a weekend news flow this report cannot see. AGAINST all of that: open interest is 2,085,556,502 USD, down 1.15 percent since midday and down 3.77 percent from the morning peak, funding is essentially zero at -0.00040 percent, and the OKX 1H account ratio is 1.06. The leverage that caused the midday flush has genuinely left the market and has NOT rebuilt on this bounce, which is the single best argument that a Sunday-night fade would be shallow rather than another 800-point break. The 79,640.0 resting stop exists precisely because I do not get to make that judgement at 03:00.

liquidation.note: 813,202 USD across 96 fills, ALL of it SHORT - not one long fill in the bucket. This is the entire story of the last hour: between 23:38 and 00:19 UTC price ran from 80,046.4 to 80,555.4 and emptied a short pocket that had been building since the 03 September push. It is by a wide margin the most one-sided cluster this series has recorded in either direction, and it is the mirror image of what happened at midday, when 653,398 USD of 100-percent-LONG fills printed at 79,500 on the way to 79,199.0. Magnet stays TRUE because the level defines where the forced buyers were, but it has already fired - price is now 358.6 points BELOW it with the fuel spent, which is why the add gate sits above the high rather than at it.

8 USD across a single short fill. Effectively nothing, and worth stating precisely because it is the level immediately above spot: there is no pocket between 80,141.4 and 80,500 for price to be pulled into. The path up from here is unassisted.

3,305 USD across 3 fills, all LONG. The only long liquidation activity in the entire 41-minute window, and it is trivial in size - 0.4 percent of what the shorts paid above. Two readings are possible and both are benign for the immediate downside: either the longs that bought this bounce are not leveraged, or they are not yet offside. The larger long shelves from earlier today - 653,398 USD at 79,500 and 147,959 USD at 79,250 - are more than six hours old and have already been consumed, so they are context rather than live levels.

liquidityMagnet.note: Genuinely balanced, and unusually so. The cluster above is 246 times larger than the one below in USD terms, which would normally read as a strong upward pull - except it has already fired and is therefore spent, not pending. The cluster below is negligible. Funding at -0.00040 percent is fractionally NEGATIVE, meaning shorts are paying longs and the perp trades at a slight discount to spot, while the OKX 1H account ratio at 1.06 says the account base is only mildly long-tilted. So the derivatives book is not crowded in either direction after a day that flushed both sides. That is a market with no obvious magnet and therefore one that will take its direction from whatever news arrives overnight rather than from positioning - which is exactly the condition in which a resting stop earns its keep.

calibration.rollingRecord: Settled-close gates: 24 correct out of the last 25 evaluated sessions, with two rows backfilled this run. Midday's 79,915.0 add gate FIRED and fired correctly: the 18:00 UTC candle settled 79,949.5, 34.5 points through the trigger, and price went on to print 80,555.4 - 605.9 points of follow-through. This morning's midnight row is also resolved and both of its gates refused correctly (reduce 79,455.0 against a lowest settled close of 79,851.9; add 80,230.0 against a highest settled close of 80,001.2). calibration.note: Acting HELPED this time, and it is worth being precise about which part. Midday added a 4 USDT spot tranche at 79,767.6 into the tail of the forced-selling flush; spot is 80,141.4, so that tranche is up 0.47 percent and the whole spot core gained roughly 1.0 USDT on the mark. The reasoning midday gave - that the leverage had genuinely left rather than rotated, evidenced by open interest falling 2.65 percent and the account ratio dropping 1.11 to 1.05 - was correct and the price expressed it within seven hours. Set against yesterday's record this matters: morning's identical logic at 79,910.1 was structurally right and got expressed 700 points lower. Same thesis, two different fills, opposite outcomes. The lesson the ledger should keep is about entry location under a shared thesis, not about the thesis. One honest caveat on this run's own decision: I am trimming 12 percent of that same core one session after buying it, which looks contradictory. It is not a change of view - it is that the wallet has 3.88 USDT of cash going into a six-and-a-half-hour gap, and cash is a position too.
